Onthe cocktail list, find drinks like Beet theHeat (made with spicy pisco and beetsyrup) and Amarillo Passion (in whichtequila meets yuzu liqueur, passion fruitsyrup, and the aji amarillo chile).
647 Tremont St., South End, Boston,617-286-2333, www.desnudacoci-na.com. Smaller plates $6-$18, largerplates $18-$32, cocktails $14-$17.
Kaia

The latest from Xenia Greek Hospi-tality, which brought us Bar Vlaha, Kra-si, and more. This time, culinary direc-tor Brendan Pelley and team whisk din-ers to the Aegean (with a South Endmind-set) via dishes like sea bream cru-do with fermented squash broth; barleytoasts with beets, pears, and vegan feta;black truffle spanakopita; and grilledwhole fish. The wine list is devoted sole-ly to selections from the Aegean andEastern Mediterranean islands.
370 Harrison Ave., South End, Bos-ton, 617-514-0700, www.kaiasouth-end.com. Dishes $16-$44.
Masons Steakhouse

Here's what happens when a groupof powerhouse South Shore culinarypros (including Jimmy Liang of JP FujiGroup and Kevin Long of Tosca) joinforces. This swank Quincy steakhouse islocated in a former Masonic temple andserves up lobster bisque, oysters Rocke-feller, pappardelle bolognese, salmonwith spiced cauliflower — and, ofcourse, beautiful steaks. The also-beau-tiful, creative desserts are from pastrychef and Masons co-owner Robert Gon-zalez, who is behind Quincy's NiveauxPâtisserie. In a landscape (increasingly)stocked with steakhouses, it is nice tosee a new one open with local owner-ship.
1170 Hancock St., Quincy, 617-689-8818, www.masonssteakhouse.com. Ap-petizers $14-$32, entrees $29-$45,steaks $52-$160, sides $6-$14, desserts$12-$19.
McGonagle's Pub

If you appreciate the Dubliner,bringing excellent fish and chips andIrish hospitality to downtown Boston,you will likely feel the same about McG-onagle's in Dorchester. Pigs in a blanketmade with sausage from Adams Village

Butcher Shop, smoky seafood chowderwith Irish soda bread, shepherd's pie,bangers and mash, and other pub favor-ites are here, along with wood-fired piz-za, brunch (yes, full Irish breakfast),and festive cocktails. Or just drop in forlive music and a proper pint of Guin-ness.
367 Neponset Ave., Dorchester, 617-514-4689, www.mcgonagles.com. Appe-tizers $8-$16, pizza $18-$19, entrees$18-$34.
Mikiya Wagyu Shabu House

If you're starving, cold, and enjoywagyu beef, Mikiya is calling you. ThisChinatown restaurant serves all-you-can-eat wagyu hot pot at a variety ofprice points; you have 90 minutes tocook a variety of cuts in the broths ofyour choosing, while eating specialtydishes such as sweet shrimp sashimiand wagyu bone marrow, plus fruit andice cream for dessert. Mikiya is a projectfrom Chubby Group, whose Kevin Liu isalso behind Matsunori Handroll Bar.
Wagyu sets $45-$98 (less with annu-al membership; free or half-price forkids).
Russ & Mimi's

Named for the parents of owner Kel-ly Walsh (Sweet Cheeks, Tiger Mama),this Roslindale market offers wine (it'sin the former Solera space), olive oil, hotsauce, and other must-haves. But it's thefood that has the neighborhood mostexcited. Start the morning with eggwraps, overnight oats, cheesy grits, andcumin-spiced black beans with friedegg, salsa, and avocado; then segue intothe “Cubano, veggie grinder, muffuletta,charred broccoli Caesar" part of the day.Chef Stephen Marcaurelle (the NautilusPier 4, Tres Gatos) helped design themenu.
16 Birch St., Roslindale, 617-833-6950, www.russandmimis.com. Dishes
Soul on Shawmut

Roxbury-raised chef Aadam Abdul-Musawwir began serving preparedmeals and pop-up dinners as Aadam'sHalal Meals. Now, he and two siblingshave opened Soul on Shawmut to feedtheir community. Lightly updated soulfood classics are on the menu, alongwith Buffalo chicken egg rolls, grilledcheese burgers, and more. Fried chick-en with Old Bay honey, smoked macand cheese, slow-cooked collard greenswith sauteed cabbage, sweet potatocheesecake, and hibiscus watermelonjuice sounds pretty unbeatable for din-ner tonight.
722A Shawmut Ave., Roxbury, 617-238-7525, www.soulonshawmut.com.Sandwiches $10-$18, fried chicken$7-$18, sides $5, desserts $3-$6.
Standard Italian

Where others fail, there is Italianfood. Standard Italian, in the EasternStandard complex looming over Fen-way, replaces the former All That Fish +Oyster, and it's a smart move. Lasagnabolognese, porchetta, and espressomartinis could just get us all throughthe winter. Culinary director Brian Raeis in his element, having previouslyworked at Coppa, Faccia a Faccia, andRialto.
771 Beacon St., Fenway, Boston, 857-305-3095, www.standarditalian.com.Appetizers $5-$20, entrees $28-$42, des-serts $9-$12.
Zurito

It's named for the small glass of beerthat often accompanies pintxos, theBasque take on tapas, and this BeaconHill restaurant serves up plenty: Gildas,skewers of anchovies, peppers, and ol-ives; griddled shrimp with garlic andchile oil; mini croissants stuffed with ja-mon iberico; squid ink risotto. Cocktailssuch as the sherry-based Perfect Bam-boo and fizzy glasses of tzakolina areperfect accompaniments. Zurito, locat-ed in the longtime Bin 26 space, is runby chef Jamie Bissonnette, Babak Bina,and Andy Cartin of BCB3 Hospitality, al-so behind Somaek, Temple Records,and Sushi @ Temple Records.
26 Charles St., Beacon Hill, Boston,857-305-3177, www.zuritoboston.com.Pintxos $4.50-$12, raciones $9-$19,platos especiales $17-$125.
Restaurants continue to innovate in mocktail realm
MOCKTAILS
Continued from Page G1

there are a plethora of base op-tions that can really make a non-alcoholic drink look and tastenearly identical to an alcoholicone," says Joel Atlas, a mixologistat the Avery Bar at the Ritz-Carl-ton, Boston. "The bloom of op-tions has really picked up in thelast year and a half to two years."

"[Mocktails] are certainlymarketed more in January, butthe truth of it all is that the non-alcoholic or low-ABV consumeris sustaining through much ofthe year," says Nick Moniz, gen-eral manager of Banners Kitch-en and Tap and Hub Hall.
"For so long, a mocktail waslimited to just a soda water andcranberry, or a sugar bomb ofjuices made with whatever waslying around behind the bar.Consumers wanted and de-served more than that."
In that spirit — or lack there-of — here are 12 mocktail desti-nations to try every month of theyear.
Abe & Louie's

The storied steakhouse offersa $14 mocktail menu. Their NewYear, New Spritz combines zero-proof sparkling Cava with non-alcoholic tequila, cucumber,lime, and mint for a spa-likepour. Good for: expense-accountdining. 793 Boylston St., Boston,617-536-6300
Alcove

In the West End, cozy Alcovedoes an $11 mocktail menu withunusual offerings like Papi'sPunch, with grilled pineapplesyrup and Athletic Free Wavenonalcoholic IPA, or a Queen'sBee, made with the herbaceousnonalcoholic spirit Garden 108and honey. Good for: T.D. Gar-den pre-game hangouts. 50 Love-joy Wharf, Boston, 617-248-0050
Avery Bar at the Ritz-Carlton,Boston

This might be one of Boston'smost classic of cocktail refuges,but it also caters to modern mo-res. A nonalcoholic Old-Fash-ioned employs decaf Englishbreakfast tea; a Cucumber Gim-less is an aromatic booze-freegin-and-cucumber palate cleans-er. Good for: sophisticated post-work drinks. 10 Avery St., Bos-ton, 617-574-7176
Baleia

This stylish new Portugueserestaurant in the South End,from the team behind Gufo andSRV, welcomes a cosmopolitancrowd eager to experiment withnonalcoholic delights. Try theTropical Amargo, an aperitifmade with coconut-chai, orange,lime, pineapple, and coffee, plusspirit-free Campari. Good for:date night. 264 East Berkeley St.,Boston, 617-505-3243
Bistro du Midi
This French restaurant enjoysa scenic perch overlooking the
Above: Warming mocktailsat Capo in South Boston.Left: A cosmopolitan atBistro du Midi.

Public Garden, and it serves farmore than wine. A $10 mocktailmenu has spins on classics like ti-ki punch, a cosmopolitan, and aspicy citrus mule. Good for: din-ner with the parents. 272 Boyl-ston St., Boston, 617-279-8000
Capo

This South Boston red-saucelair might seem like the type ofspot to throw back icy martinis(they do host Sinatra Sundays, af-ter all) paired with big plates ofrigatoni Bolognese, but they alsohave warming $9 mocktails, likethe Far From the Tree, withtoasty apple cider, cardamom,allspice, thyme, and egg whites.In addition to catering to non-drinkers, they accommodate arange of palates, with gluten-freepasta on request. Good for: anight out with a group. 443 WestBroadway, Boston, 617-993-8080
Hunter's

This is your spot for biscuits,fried chicken, mac-and-cheese ...in other words, resolution-breaking meals. That said: Thisdark, cozy bar and kitchen alsopays attention to mocktails,which are a relative steal at $6.Wash down your honey-butter,bacon-topped cornbread withrefreshing house-made water-melon juice and soda. Good for:comfort food. 110 Dorchester St,Boston, 617-221-4200
La Padrona

Stylish, swanky, and with astellar chef attached (Jody Ad-ams), this Italian destination in-side Raffles Boston is the ulti-mate in special-occasion dining:The silken tagliatelle alone isworth the trip up that grandstaircase. Sure, there's also an ex-tensive martini menu, but spirit-free drinks also get proper due.A nonalcoholic tangerine marga-rita with spirit-free tequila andlime is worth toasting. Not quiteready to abstain? There's also anextensive low-ABV list featuringtreats like a Lambrusco Cobbler,made with black currant andberries. Good for: a celebratorysplurge. 38 Trinity Place, Boston,617-221-4200
Midnight Morning

This cheery Roslindale bistrospecializes in comfort food: sau-sage dip, mushroom-and-cream-cheese wontons, burgers, andfried pickles. It makes nondrink-ers feel comfy, too, with a nice$12 selection of zero-proofdrinks: The Regret Nothing,with nonalcoholic Ritual Prooftequila, jalapeno, and lime, istrue to its name. Good for: a laid-back weeknight dinner. 14 BirchSt., Roslindale, 617-390-5830
Trina's Starlite Lounge

This industry hangout takesdive-bar food to another level —they pioneered dressed-up tatertots and mac-and-cheese beforeit was fashionable. Here, $5 cansof Miller High Life share real es-tate with cheeky mocktails likethe Phony Negroni, a nonalco-holic version of the classic, andIsland Life, Baby, made with abooze-free, floral Fluère BotanicBlend. Good for: dive-bar-diningwithout the buzz. 3 Beacon St.,Somerville, 617-576-0006
Tuscan Brands

This Italian mini-empireserves reliable food in conve-nient locations and a thoughtful-ly curated list of spirit-free sips,like a Tea Party with coconut wa-ter, chai tea, and brown sugar,and the Cos-No-Politan, madewith honey water, cranberry,rooibos tea, and lime. Beveragedirector Jose Luis Betancur alsohas a fondness for tart Italian so-das like Chinotto or Stappi Gas-sosa. Good for: pleasing a crowd(or kids). 64 Seaport Boulevard,Boston, 617-303-7300, and otherlocations
